EO 12902 (1994) revoked EO 12759 except sections 3, 9 and 10; the whole-order end is by EO 13123 (1999); exact effective dates remain lifecycle questions.
notice: Producer research decision only. Independent review and owner adoption remain separate.
rationale: I read the complete held EO 12759 original (56 FR 16257, Federal Energy Management, April 17, 1991): policy sections on energy efficiency goals with no own sunset, termination or expiry term. I read the held EO 12902 text (the part 7 revocation section 701, held text carries a page-check flag so I did not use it as basis): 'Executive Order No. 12759 ... is hereby revoked, except that sections 3, 9, and 10 of that order shall remain effective and shall not be revoked.' That was therefore only a partial revocation. I read the held EO 13123 text (64 FR, June 3, 1999): section 604 'Executive Order 12902 of March 9, 1994, Executive Order 12759 of April 17, 1991, and Executive Order 12845 ... are revoked', unqualified and with no exception preserving sections 3, 9 or 10. That ends the surviving sections as well. No savings clause in EO 13123 for EO 12759 was found. The catalog note lists both revoking orders; the earlier partial revocation does not change the whole-order result. Provisional NO hypothesis; later revocations of EO 13123 do not revive EO 12759 and no revival text was seen.
